markdown_report:
The strongest next step is a **catalog competition audit** of each category’s single NextItNet checkpoint. At 0% research progress, this is a feasible investigation of training fit and candidate competition. Its ability to guide improvements in pinned validation HR@10 remains unproven.

Three insights follow from the supplied diagnosis. First, Electronics has 9.38% negative-over-positive outcomes, versus 0.23–3.91% elsewhere. This indicates weaker measured training separation, without establishing poorer generalization. Second, frequency-matched old substitutions are less disruptive than random substitutions in Movies and CDs. Their absolute margin changes remain negative, providing no evidence that removing older history improves recommendations. Third, observed padding activations were zero. Locality remains uncertified, requiring further dependency checks.

Three literature insights refine the investigation. Krichene–Rendle show that sampled metrics can reverse catalog comparisons, so the two measurements must remain distinct. Prakash et al. motivate frequency strata; Dong et al. distinguish memorization from generalization. Li et al. distinguish repeat and first-time prediction, requiring explicit candidate populations and history filtering.

These insights define three directions:

| Direction | Measurement | Remaining gap |
|---|---|---|
| Competition | Catalog training-target ranks | Generalization and benchmark alignment |
| Temporal mechanism | Controlled lag or activation intervention | Whether retraining helps |
| Evidence sufficiency | Title/description support and abstention | Actual intent or satisfaction |

Three atomic ideas merit consideration. Scores are originality/potential/difficulty; higher difficulty means more implementation work.

| Idea | Scores | Positive and negative assessments |
|---|---|---|
| Catalog competition audit [1,2,6,7] | 4/6/5 | Originality: useful integration, established components. Potential: identifies competition, predictive value for validation is unproven. Difficulty: existing scoring interface helps, event identity and numerical consistency require care. |
| Block activation patching [3,4] | 5/6/6 | Originality: family-specific adaptation, established intervention. Potential: localizes sensitivity, restoration does not prove necessity. Difficulty: hooks avoid retraining, downstream recomputation needs controls. |
| Evidence-and-abstention records [5] | 4/6/4 | Originality: useful adaptation, existing annotation principles. Potential: separates unsupported claims, cannot recover latent intent. Difficulty: public text suffices, annotation needs calibration. |

Select the **catalog competition audit**. Freeze each model; sample identifiable training events with strictly preceding contexts. Report repeat-capable prediction separately from unseen-target retrieval, whose exclusions use complete pre-target histories. Gather the final nonpadding feature and stream catalog scores in fixed chunks. Extract target scores from their actual chunks, replay identical chunks, and count higher scores and exact ties. Verify streaming results against materialized scores on a small subset [8–10].

Compare ranks and target-minus-tenth-competitor margins with supplied-negative separation, reporting frequency/length strata, event counts, and user counts. Deduplicate event identities and disclose event weighting. Preserve diagnostic interfaces, four-category routing, and one checkpoint per category. These are fitting diagnostics: only pinned host macro validation HR@10 selects models. Any later one-factor training change requires validation; no additional predictor or inferred compatibility signal is introduced.

References [1–10] and their limitations appear below.

idea.description: Add a bounded catalog competition audit to the existing family-aware NextItNet diagnostic adapter. For reproducible, identifiable training events, compare supplied-negative separation with target ranks under explicitly defined repeat-capable and unseen-target catalog protocols using the same frozen checkpoint. Report frequency and history-length strata without fitting another predictor. Ranks are exact for the disclosed computed scores and candidate eligibility; exact tie-resolved ranks require an explicit total ordering.
idea.motivation: The supplied measurements show substantial differences in training pairwise separation, particularly Electronics’ 9.38% negative-over-positive rate. They do not reveal how many catalog items outrank an observed target. Previous lag interventions establish relative temporal sensitivity rather than harmful older history. Catalog competition offers a complementary diagnostic, but available evidence does not establish that improving catalog training ranks improves pinned sampled-candidate validation HR@10. Separating repeat and unseen targets, controlling numerical comparisons, and tracking event identity prevents misleading conclusions. Qualitative feedback remains a hypothesis source rather than evidence of ownership, compatibility, or intent.
idea.implementation_notes:
Retain DiagnosisProbe(view, device), run_full_diagnosis(train_loader), and diagnosis_interpreter_prompt(raw_diagnosis). Return metrics and metric_definitions; distinguish training-event catalog measurements from host validation metrics. Preserve view.model, item_emb, log2feats(sequence), predict_score(features, items), user_train, meta_data, and review_data interfaces. Use only public histories, timestamps, titles, and descriptions. Item categories, ratings, review text, prices, stores, and simulator traits remain unavailable.

Use only training histories and aligned next-training-item targets. Cache at most ten loader batches and reproducibly select at most 128 valid unique events per category using a local seed-42 generator. Identify each event by category, training user ID, and target endpoint in that user's training history. Match the encoded prefix and aligned target to stored histories; exclude ambiguous matches with counts rather than assigning guessed identities. Collapse repeated sampling of the same event, while retaining distinct real events even when their encoded sequences match. Record complete pre-target histories from that identified event, never from post-target interactions. If reliable event identities cannot be recovered, mark the event audit unavailable; an optional window-only row audit must be labeled separately and cannot claim complete-history filtering or user-level uncertainty.

Construct the eligible event pool before sampling. Define target-frequency bands from all training interactions only, using empirical quintile boundaries and assigning equal frequencies together; report actual boundaries and bin sizes. Define encoded-prefix-length strata 1–5, 6–15, 16–31, and 32+. Allocate the 128-event cap evenly across nonempty frequency-by-length cells, capped by cell capacity; redistribute remaining slots in fixed cell order. Sample without replacement within cells using the local generator. Report pool sizes, selected counts, and inclusion probabilities. Primary summaries are event-weighted descriptions of the selected stratified sample, not estimates of the natural training-event distribution. Any population-weighted estimate must explicitly use the recorded inclusion probabilities. Report empty cells and exclusions. The cap and strata are prespecified resource choices, not established optima.

Save and restore the actual module's training mode, disable gradients, and score in evaluation/inference mode. Gather features at the largest occupied sequence index, never occupied_count-1. Exclude empty histories, invalid catalog IDs, and invalid aligned targets with explicit counts. Confirm that each target follows the reconstructed input prefix. Targets may already have influenced parameter fitting; causal inference inputs do not make these held-out observations.

Report two candidate protocols separately. Repeat-capable next-item prediction includes every valid catalog ID, including previously seen items, and excludes padding; report repeat and first-time targets separately. Unseen-target retrieval excludes events whose target appears anywhere in the complete pre-target history, then excludes all previously seen catalog items from candidates. Report excluded repeat events and eligible denominators. The earlier proposal's prefix-window exclusion with target retention may remain as an explicitly named optional window-filtered diagnostic; it does not represent complete-history unseen retrieval, because older consumed items can re-enter the candidate set. Do not combine the protocols into a single unlabeled summary.

For supplied-negative comparisons require a valid, distinct negative. Preserve and report the original supplied-negative margin separately. Add an eligibility flag under each catalog protocol and report a paired comparison restricted to eligible supplied negatives. Do not silently replace invalid negatives or claim that supplied-negative and catalog ranks estimate the same quantity. If later extending to multiple diagnostic negatives, remove target collisions and duplicates, document filtering, and report realized candidate counts. Never modify host validation candidates.

Use predict_score in bounded catalog chunks, for example width 4,096 and a fixed user-batch size of 16, avoiding a users-by-entire-catalog allocation. Define the catalog as sorted valid integer IDs 1 through view.model.itemnum. Freeze features once. First score every chunk and extract each target's score from its actual catalog chunk before eligibility masking. Replay exactly the same chunks, feature batch, ordering, padding policy, dtype, and scoring calls to count eligible competitors. Do not compare separately computed target dot products with matrix-scored competitors. Report chunk and batch dimensions, including final partial shapes. Exact equality means equality of the computed scores; tolerance-based equality would define a different ranking protocol.

For a diagnostic FP32 audit, disable autocast and TF32, disable cuDNN benchmarking, and request deterministic algorithms. Configure CUBLAS_WORKSPACE_CONFIG=:4096:8 before CUDA initialization in the host entry point when possible; the adapter must not claim to establish it after initialization. Record hardware, PyTorch/CUDA versions, precision settings, and unsupported deterministic operations. Restore process-level settings after the audit where safe. These controls repeat fixed computations; they do not guarantee invariance across GEMM shapes. Score and rank checks across selected chunk widths, user-batch sizes, and partial final chunks are numerical-sensitivity checks. The primary result always uses the disclosed fixed configuration. A canonical fixed-reduction kernel is necessary only if strict shape invariance becomes a requirement; it is outside this minimal proposal.

Excluding the target itself, accumulate greater=count(score>target_score), ties=count(score==target_score), and eligible candidate counts. Report possible one-based target ranks [1+greater, 1+greater+ties], corresponding top-10 hit bounds, and normalized ranks (rank-1)/(eligible_count-1), with singleton catalogs explicitly missing. These are diagnostic tie bounds; do not infer the host tie rule. Maintain the ten highest eligible competitor scores to compute target-minus-tenth-competitor margin; mark it missing when fewer than ten alternatives exist. For competitor identities use descending score then ascending item ID consistently, rather than relying on torch.topk's tied-index ordering. Reject nonfinite features, target scores, or eligible competitor scores with counted reasons.

Validate streaming counters, exclusions, repeat handling, duplicate-event handling, and ties against materialized candidate scores for a small selected subset using the identical chunk computations. Include synthetic score-array checks for ties and fewer than ten alternatives without fitting additional models. A single full-matrix GEMM can produce slightly different scores; treat that comparison as a numerical-sensitivity check rather than an unquestioned reference. FP64 recomputation can diagnose near-tie sensitivity but cannot establish the original FP32 rank.

Report rank quantiles, normalized-rank bounds, training-event HR@10 bounds, target-minus-tenth-competitor margins, original supplied-negative margins, eligible-negative paired summaries, target frequencies, and distinct event/user counts. Compare supplied-negative win rates with catalog competition on the same eligible observations. Optional competitor IDs, scores, training frequencies, and top-10 popularity concentration are descriptive diagnostics. Unobserved competitors are not confirmed negatives, and popularity counts do not identify exposure propensities or dislikes. Aggregate categories with equal category weights only for explicitly named training diagnostics; never label them validation results.

If uncertainty is reported, use 2,000 user-cluster bootstrap replicates with local seed 42, retaining each sampled user's selected events together and recomputing the declared event-weighted statistic. Disclose that intervals condition on the selected events, checkpoint, candidate protocol, and numerical configuration; they exclude training-seed, adaptive-search, and stratified-event-sampling uncertainty. Do not claim simultaneous guarantees across strata or categories. With insufficient identifiable users, omit intervals and give a reason.

Training targets can be memorized, and popularity shortcuts can produce strong training ranks. This audit adds no learned shortcut itself, but adapting a model repeatedly to its outputs can overfit the search process. Do not optimize diagnostic scores as an objective. A later optional longitudinal extension may inspect three prespecified snapshots of the same training trajectory, without averaging their predictions or deploying multiple checkpoints; it is outside the initial bounded audit. Improving training fit with flat validation would motivate a one-factor regularization trial, while weak separation might motivate more negatives with training-observation collision filtering. Neither outcome proves its proposed remedy. Avoid automatically treating hard examples as noise or high-ranked unobserved items as disliked. Any training change must retain one jointly trained NextItNet model per category and be selected solely by pinned four-category macro validation HR@10.

Keep the supplied corrected cold-start NextItNet training and predictor writer unchanged for this diagnostic-only proposal. Preserve all four routes, DATA_DIR=os.environ['GAGC_DATA_DIR'], trial-local artifacts, preprocessing seed 0, training seed 42, maximum 200 epochs, 200 batches per epoch, and single-GPU execution. Prediction loads exactly one independently trained checkpoint per category. Any later architecture change must update the embedded predictor writer consistently. Bound audit work by the fixed event, batch, and chunk configuration; record elapsed diagnostic runtime within the shared 43,200 GPU-second budget. Do not reconstruct hidden validation candidates, access test data, reuse other trials, or introduce score fusion. No implementation, training run, or new measurement was executed for this proposal.
idea.pseudocode:
def run_full_diagnosis(self, train_loader):
    previous_mode = self.view.model.training
    metrics, definitions = {}, {}
    previous_precision = capture_precision_settings()
    try:
        self.view.model.eval()
        configure_recorded_fp32_audit_settings()
        # CUDA environment settings must already be configured before initialization.
        cached = cache_batches(train_loader, maximum=10)
        events = identify_training_events(cached, self.view.user_train)
        # Identity = (category, user_id, target_endpoint); reject ambiguous matches.
        events = deduplicate_event_identities(events)
        validate_strictly_preceding_contexts(events)
        frequency_bands = tied_quintile_bands_from_training_histories()
        events = stratified_sample_without_replacement(
            events, frequency_bands, length_bands=[5, 15, 31],
            maximum=128, local_seed=42,
            allocation='balanced_cells_then_fixed_order_redistribution')
        record_pool_sizes_selection_probabilities_and_exclusions()

        with torch.inference_mode():
            for batch in fixed_user_batches(events, size=16):
                last = largest_original_occupied_index(batch.sequence)
                validate_nonempty_sequences_and_aligned_targets(batch, last)
                features = gather_sequence_features(
                    self.view.log2feats(batch.sequence), last)
                chunks = fixed_sorted_catalog_chunks(
                    first_id=1, last_id=self.view.model.itemnum, width=4096)

                # Pass 1: target scores come from actual catalog scoring calls.
                target_scores = empty_target_score_vector(batch)
                for items in chunks:
                    scores = self.view.predict_score(features, items)
                    extract_target_scores_before_masking(
                        scores, items, batch.target, target_scores)
                mark_nonfinite_target_or_feature_rows()

                counters = initialize_per_protocol_counters()
                for items in chunks:
                    # Replay identical feature batch, shapes, order, and calls.
                    scores = self.view.predict_score(features, items)
                    for protocol in ['repeat_capable', 'unseen_target']:
                        event_eligible, item_eligible = eligibility(
                            protocol, items, batch.target,
                            complete_pre_target_history=batch.pre_target_history)
                        # Unseen protocol excludes repeat-target events entirely.
                        alternatives = item_eligible & (items != batch.target)
                        reject_nonfinite_eligible_rows_with_counts(scores)
                        counters[protocol].update(
                            greater=count(scores > target_scores, alternatives),
                            ties=count(scores == target_scores, alternatives),
                            eligible=count(item_eligible),
                            top10_competitors=stable_top10(
                                scores, items, alternatives,
                                ordering='score_desc_item_id_asc'))

                record_rank_bounds_and_tenth_competitor_margins(counters)
                record_repeat_and_first_time_strata()
                record_original_valid_distinct_supplied_negative_margins(batch)
                record_protocol_eligible_negative_comparisons(batch)
                record_frequency_length_event_and_user_counts(batch)

        validate_streaming_against_materialized_identical_chunk_scores(
            small_subset=True, include_ties_exclusions_and_repeat_cases=True)
        report_bounded_shape_sensitivity_checks_separately()
        summarize_selected_sample_with_explicit_event_weighting()
        optional_user_cluster_bootstrap(replicates=2000, local_seed=42)
        define_every_metric_population_filter_tie_rule_and_missing_reason()
    finally:
        restore_precision_settings(previous_precision)
        self.view.model.train(previous_mode)
    return {'metrics': metrics, 'metric_definitions': definitions}

# diagnosis_interpreter_prompt(raw_diagnosis) embeds both dictionaries;
# requests evidence-linked findings; labels catalog results as training fit;
# distinguishes repeat, unseen, and optional window-filtered populations;
# prohibits inferred intent, exposure propensities, or validation improvements.

originality.positive: Combines family-specific diagnostics, explicit repeat/unseen populations, event identity, and numerically consistent streaming rank bounds in one practical adapter.
originality.negative: Exact ranking, stratification, clustered uncertainty, and numerical controls are established techniques; novelty lies in their integration.

future_potential.positive: Can expose catalog competition and frequency-dependent fitting that supplied-negative margins miss, motivating targeted single-model experiments.
future_potential.negative: There is no direct evidence that these training diagnostics predict pinned NextItNet validation HR@10 gains; memorization and evaluator mismatch limit their decision value.

code_difficulty.positive: Existing ModelView scoring methods suffice, and the initial audit requires no retraining, architecture change, or additional fitted predictor.
code_difficulty.negative: Reliable event reconstruction, complete pre-target filtering, two-pass scoring, numerical checks, and aggregation make this more demanding than a basic catalog scan.

related_work.title: On Sampled Metrics for Item Recommendation
contributions: Shows that sampled ranking metrics can disagree with full-catalog comparisons.
Motivates separating supplied-negative separation, catalog training competition, and the pinned sampled-candidate validation objective.
limitations: Does not establish that catalog training diagnostics predict held-out performance.
Does not justify altering the pinned host evaluator.

related_work.title: Prakash et al.: sequential recommendation, negative sampling, and popularity imbalance
contributions: The supplied search summary reports performance differences across item-frequency groups and sensitivity to negative sampling.
Motivates frequency strata alongside aggregate margins.
limitations: These findings are not measurements of the supplied NextItNet checkpoints.
Frequency counts cannot establish individual intent, exposure propensity, or dislike.

related_work.title: NextItNet
contributions: Uses residual causal dilated convolutions for sequential recommendation.
Provides the required backbone family; the supplied report also links its paper at https://fajieyuan.github.io/papers/nextitnet6.pdf.
limitations: Architecture alone does not certify every functional dependency in a modified implementation.
Does not validate the proposed catalog audit or its relationship to held-out HR@10 gains.

related_work.title: Heimersheim and Nanda: activation patching guidance
contributions: Distinguishes restoration and disruption interpretations of activation patching.
Informs the alternative block-patching direction.
limitations: Transfer to sequential recommendation requires validation.
Restoration does not prove necessity or unique information storage.

related_work.title: Evidence relevance and sufficiency annotation protocol
contributions: The supplied search summary describes separating relevance, support, and insufficient evidence.
Informs recommendation evidence records that explicitly allow abstention.
limitations: Is not a validated Amazon recommendation rubric.
Text annotations cannot establish ownership, satisfaction, or latent purchasing needs.

related_work.title: Dong et al.: memorization, generalization, and subgroup performance
contributions: The supplied search summary distinguishes memorization, generalization, and subgroup performance.
Supports labeling fitted training-target ranks separately from held-out evaluation.
limitations: Does not establish that the proposed NextItNet diagnostic predicts validation improvement.
A subgroup training-fit difference alone does not identify its cause.

related_work.title: Li et al.: repetition in recommendation
contributions: Distinguishes previously consumed targets from first-time targets.
Motivates separate repeat-capable and unseen-target populations with explicit history filtering.
limitations: Does not determine the pinned benchmark's eligibility rules.
Its findings do not justify changing benchmark candidates or filtering.

related_work.title: PyTorch numerical accuracy
contributions: Explains that mathematically equivalent computations can differ across batching and computation shapes.
Supports extracting target scores from actual catalog chunks and reporting numerical sensitivity.
limitations: FP32 and deterministic settings do not guarantee chunk-size-invariant scores.
Higher-precision recomputation changes the numerical computation rather than certifying the original ranking.

related_work.title: PyTorch reproducibility
contributions: Documents deterministic-algorithm controls and reproducibility limitations.
Supports recording precision settings, software, hardware, and initialization-time CUDA configuration.
limitations: Does not guarantee reproducibility across releases, devices, or platforms.
Determinism for a fixed computation does not establish equality across GEMM shapes.

related_work.title: PyTorch topk
contributions: Documents that tied indices returned by topk are not guaranteed to be stable.
Motivates a consistent score-and-item-ID total ordering when reporting competitor identities.
limitations: A diagnostic ordering cannot be assumed to match the host evaluator's tie rule.
Tolerance-based ties would change the ranking definition.

related_work.title: Denoising Implicit Feedback
contributions: The supplied search summary describes adaptive loss weighting motivated by noisy implicit interactions.
Offers a possible later one-factor regularization hypothesis.
limitations: High loss alone cannot establish that a sparse interaction is noise.
Does not justify automatically dropping difficult training targets.

related_work.title: UFNRec
contributions: The supplied search summary reports benefits from addressing false negatives in sequential recommendation.
Motivates caution when interpreting unobserved catalog competitors.
limitations: Its teacher-based implementation should not be imported into the mandatory single-model experiment.
Training-history collision filtering cannot identify all genuine false negatives.

related_work.title: Recommendations as Treatments: Debiasing Learning and Evaluation
contributions: Establishes selection-bias concerns in recommendation learning and evaluation.
Supports distinguishing observed popularity from exposure and preference.
limitations: Popularity counts alone do not identify exposure propensities.
The proposed audit does not estimate causal preferences or correct selection bias.

related_work.title: Reproducible recommender evaluation
contributions: The supplied search summary emphasizes explicit evaluation populations, sampling, and implementation choices.
Motivates publishing seeds, candidate rules, denominators, and aggregation.
limitations: Reproducibility does not establish generalization or causal validity.
A reproducible diagnostic still measures a different population from pinned host validation.

related_work.title: cuBLAS reproducibility
contributions: Documents conditions and configuration relevant to reproducible CUDA matrix computations.
Supports configuring and recording workspace settings before CUDA initialization.
limitations: Does not establish equality across different matrix shapes.
An adapter invoked after CUDA initialization cannot claim to have established initialization-time controls.

related_work.title: Rendle: sampled recommendation evaluation
contributions: The supplied search summary highlights that sampling can reverse model comparisons.
Reinforces treating sampled and full-catalog measurements as distinct estimands.
limitations: Does not authorize substituting catalog diagnostics for the required sampled validation objective.
Does not establish a NextItNet-specific diagnostic-to-generalization relationship.
